clues: This mill town in Russia stands on the east side of the south Ural hills. It sits right by the banks of the Ural River.
Winters here bite far harder than its place on the map would suggest. No large sea stands near this town to soften the deep cold.
It was built as a planned town of the Soviet bloc in the Cold War days. Just a few such towns were ever made in that style.
It is home to the largest iron and steel works in Russia. A nearby hill was once made of almost pure iron ore.
Its proud motto calls it the place where Europe and Asia meet. The town sits astride the line that is said to split the two.
